inspection: Actual new END viewed with view_image; compared against the previously viewed actual START and source. No new media generated by reviewer.
fidelity_scope: source-derived visual concept, not pixel-identical catalog photography

checks.finding: The fine high-frequency collar ribbing visible in the rejected END is removed. New END collar and torso read as a smooth matte mockup material, consistent with the broad material family of START and the source. No conspicuous new rib-knit construction is apparent in the new native-size view.

One dark front-facing crewneck, smooth collar band, similar shoulder/sleeve construction and the same broad three-part pale chest motif remain. Source-derived concept continuity is acceptable at this scope.

The neckband remains a generated reconstruction with shading/contour differences rather than a demonstrably identical scaled source. The mark retains its broad three-part arrangement, but its exact corner shapes, stroke weights, spacing and source pixel proportions are not certified. These limitations must not be represented as a catalog-fidelity pass or proof of a strict uniform image transform.

START remains a full garment on image-right, and new END is a clearly enlarged upper-front detail now more centrally composed. A continuous frontal scale and translation can connect those compositions without exposing unseen sides. Actual generated interpolation and fine-feature stability remain unverified.
Soft dark garment shading and pale background remain broadly consistent, without a conspicuous lighting-mode or color-temperature change. Exact field/exposure identity is not proven.

The new END shifts the enlarged garment farther left, occupying most of the lower-left image. START's broad left text region does not survive into END as a useful common rectangle. Use live HTML outside the media or independently measure and test a smaller shared region; do not advertise START's full left space as safe throughout the shot.

The unchanged START still loses much of the garment and chest mark under a centered x approximately 571 to1101 portrait crop. The new END mark sits close to that crop's right edge and does not solve START's failure. Use a separate portrait treatment or still/contain layout rather than a universal crop claim.
No video or device playback was inspected. The repaired still pair does not establish intermediate fidelity, loop behavior, scroll smoothness or phone performance.
